proposals.evidence: CDIAL 10066 mārayati gives the mār- kill verb; maral/marla and māryo are ordinary eastern -l and western -y past/infinitive formations. Mār-diyo contains a give light verb and is not assigned as a simple inherited stem. Reviewed comparison: marwari_bagra mārīyɔ “don't kill!, he killed” (f_635k7q3sfgana). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 12598 śṛṇoti explicitly gives Bhojpuri sunal and western suṇṇo “hear”. Eastern -l and western -y inflections can continue the hear stem; sun-lo and ambiguous sunā causative/past forms require local morphology. Reviewed comparison: dhundari_badagaon sūna “listen!, he heard” (f_pycp2aj6b7c24). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 2575 kaḥ punar gives kaun/koṇ/kuṇa “who” and Old Gujarati kuṇaïṃ instrumental. The q/k variants and final pronominal vowels preserve the family; Kalasha kura needs comparison with a different interrogative stem. Reviewed comparison: dhundari_badagaon kūṇ “who?” (f_ls3rtbwicac7y). The family link leaves local phonetic details and possible transfer between Indo-Aryan languages open; no source spelling is changed.
